name: Amelia ‘Millie’ Gade Corson
highlight: Second woman and first mother across the Channel · August 1926
biography: Amelia ‘Millie’ Gade Corson was a Danish-born American endurance swimmer and swimming instructor. She moved to the United States in 1919 and worked as a lifeguard and lifesaving instructor at the Harlem branch of the YWCA. Her early American achievements included a swim around Manhattan Island and a staged journey down the Hudson from Albany to New York in 1921.

Her first Channel attempt in 1923 ended short of the French coast. She returned in 1926 and became the second woman, and the first mother, to complete the crossing, following Gertrude Ederle’s achievement earlier that month. Her successful route ran from Cap Gris-Nez to Shakespeare Beach. The Channel record lists 15 hours and 23 minutes, with other historical accounts giving different durations.

Corson returned to public celebrations in New York and made vaudeville appearances. Her photographs, scrapbooks and swimming certificates are preserved by the Smithsonian. Her career helped demonstrate the possibilities of women’s distance swimming during the sport’s early international growth.

CSA lists 15h 23m; Dover Museum’s biography gives 15h 28m and dates the swim 27 August; the Smithsonian guide gives 15¾ hours. No start or finish clock is treated as confirmed. The selected date span and duration come from explicitly identified records, not a reconciled original log.

lines.text: CSA record 2237 supplies United States, France-to-England and 15:23. The Smithsonian collection guide supplies 27–28 August 1926 and the first-mother distinction. Dover Museum identifies Cap Gris-Nez and Shakespeare Beach but differs on duration. These historical accounts were compared; no original observer report or route chart was inspected.
